questions.q: What does this wrap-up lesson identify as the one throughline connecting all six chapters of AI/ML Foundations?
options: Memorizing the scikit-learn API
Understanding what a model is actually doing, then doing it yourself
Learning as many different algorithms as possible
Focusing exclusively on deep learning
questions.explain: The course moves from conceptual understanding (chapters 1-5) to actually building, training, and evaluating a real model yourself (chapter 6) — that progression is the throughline the recap names.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what five pieces does a good capstone README need, mirroring a real model card?
options: Only the final accuracy number
Problem, data, method, results (with real numbers), and limitations
A list of every library installed
A marketing-style summary with no numbers
questions.explain: The lesson lays out a README with exactly those five sections — the same information a real Hugging Face model card provides, just about your own project instead of someone else's.

questions.q: Why does the lesson insist on stating the test set size (n=114) next to every reported metric?
options: Because sample size is irrelevant to interpreting a metric
Because a score without its sample size is close to meaningless — the same honesty standard lesson 26 applied to a model card's self-reported eval results
Because it's a scikit-learn requirement
Because larger numbers are always more impressive
questions.explain: A metric like 98.2% accuracy means something very different computed on 114 samples versus 11,400 — disclosing n lets a reader judge how much to trust the number, the same self-reported honesty chapter 5 modeled.

questions.q: Why does the lesson explicitly call out that the capstone's results come from "one 80/20 split, not cross-validated"?
options: Because cross-validation is impossible in scikit-learn
To admit a real limitation honestly — a different random_state could move the numbers, and disclosing that makes the write-up more credible, not less
Because the split was done incorrectly and needs to be redone
Because accuracy only applies to cross-validated results
questions.explain: The lesson frames honest disclosure of limitations as a credibility signal, directly extending lesson 26's point that a model card's self-reported numbers are a strong signal but not unconditional proof.

questions.q: What course does this wrap-up lesson identify as coming next in the AI Engineer path?
options: RAG & Vector Databases
Generative AI & LLMs
AI Agents
Prompt & Context Engineering
questions.explain: The outro names Generative AI & LLMs as the next course, picking up with how large language models actually work and working directly with LLM APIs.
